slides.title: Occlusal Surface
bullets: Food debris tends to accumulate more in this part of the tooth
slides.caption: View from above

slides.title: Vestibular Surface
bullets: The surface facing the cheek or lip
Also called labial on anterior teeth and buccal on posterior teeth
slides.caption: View from the cheek side

slides.title: Lingual (Tongue-Side) Surface
bullets: In the upper jaw it is also called the palatal surface
slides.caption: View from the tongue side

slides.title: Proximal Surfaces
bullets: Mesial — the side closer to the midline of the dental arch
Distal — the side farther from the midline
slides.caption: Side view

slides.title: Key Points
bullets: Mesial and distal — toward the adjacent teeth

quiz.q: What is the chewing surface called?
quiz.explanation: The occlusal surface meets the opposing tooth during chewing.
The lingual surface faces the tongue.

quiz.q: Which proximal surface is closer to the midline of the dental arch?
quiz.explanation: The mesial surface lies on the side closer to the midline.

quiz.q: On which surface are fissures found?
quiz.explanation: Fissures (grooves) are located on the chewing surface.
The vestibular surface faces the cheek or lip.
